routesElsewhere.note: Archiving is by age and the system does it, not a person (BR-8, and the lifecycle moves an item from Published to Archived on the System's trigger alone). The website items screen offers an Archive control the lifecycle has no actor for, and the age at which items are archived is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-2). Nothing is planned for it until the school gives the age.

steps.note: One step, and it produces a draft. Whether the next act is submitting it for approval or publishing it directly is configuration the Super Admin sets, and the write reports which (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An item with no category or no body is not saved, and nothing is on the site either way.
plan.atomicity: One write: the item, its category, its date, the writer's name and any attachment. It is a draft — nothing is public, and no family or alumnus can see it (AC-3, E2, E3).

errors.note: The right is granted by the Super Admin and held by a named person rather than a role (BR-1, AC-1).
Readers filter by category and the site groups by it (BR-6).

planningRules.rule: Never write the body. The holder writes the item themselves and the wording is theirs (BR-2) — this goes out under the school's name to people who are not the school's to correct afterwards. Where the request says "you write it", emit nothing and ask for their words.
Never guess the category. Readers filter by it and the site groups by it, so an item filed under the wrong one is an item nobody finds (BR-6, E2). Offer the five and let the writer choose.

Say that this is a draft. "Put a notice up" sounds finished, and it is not — nothing is on the site until it is published, and where the school requires approval it does not go up at all until the Principal gives it.

Report whether approval is required rather than assuming either way. It is configuration the Super Admin sets, the school's own choice is not stated in the document, and it decides whether the next act is a submission or a publication (BR-3, OQ-1).
Never attach a file the request only describes. A file cannot travel in a plan — it is uploaded on the screen and named here.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: There is nothing to reverse — nothing is public. But there is also no way to discard the draft: the lifecycle moves an item from Draft only to Awaiting approval or to Published, and deletion is not offered anywhere (BR-9, E7). A draft written in error stays a draft. Say so rather than promising a tidy-up that does not exist.

The permission holder cannot approve their own item. Only the Principal can, where the Super Admin has given them that role (E8).

routesElsewhere.note: Approving publishes. The lifecycle moves an item from Awaiting approval straight to Published, and there is no approved-but-held state to sit in. Where the item should go up later, it is approved later.

steps.note: One step, and it does two things: records the approval and puts the item on the site with its date and category, readable by anybody without a login (BR-5, BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Where the website cannot be reached, neither the approval nor the publication is recorded and it is reported rather than the item appearing to have gone live (BR-10, E5).
plan.atomicity: One act. Approval and publication happen together, because the lifecycle moves an item from Awaiting approval straight to Published and there is no state between them — so a website that cannot be reached fails the whole act, and the retry is a second approval.

planningRules.rule: Say that approving publishes. It is not a sign-off that somebody else acts on later — the item is on the public site the moment this returns, read by parents, alumni and prospective families who need no login (BR-5, AC-6).
Never approve an item the acting user wrote. The permission holder cannot approve their own, and a planner that routes around it defeats the one check standing between a draft and the public (E8).

operations.name: website.item.edit
operations.idempotencyKey: item_id + the fields submitted, so a double press does not leave two identical rows in the change history
operations.purpose: Correct a published item and log the change.

parameters.name: item_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No item matches that description. Name it as it appears on the website items screen.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the items that match with their category and the date they carry.

parameters.notes: The item, named the way the writer names it — by its title, its category or the date it carries.

parameters.name: title
parameters.notes: The corrected title, where the title is what is wrong.

parameters.name: body
parameters.notes: The corrected wording, the holder's own (BR-2). Never redrafted here.

parameters.name: category
parameters.notes: Where the item was filed under the wrong one. Readers filter by it, so an item in the wrong category is an item nobody finds (BR-6).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What changed and what stands on the site now.

fields.name: item_id
fields.description: The item.

fields.name: changed
fields.description: What changed, field by field, before and after (BR-7, AC-7).

fields.name: changed_by
fields.description: Who changed it.

fields.name: changed_at
fields.description: When.

fields.name: public_url
fields.description: Where the corrected item stands.

fields.name: was_public_before
fields.description: True. Whoever read the old wording read it, and the record of what stood there is why the history is kept (BR-7).

errors.meaning: The acting user does not hold the right to publish to the website.
errors.notWritten: The item on the site is unchanged.

errors.meaning: The category was cleared rather than changed.
errors.note: Every item carries a category, and an item with none cannot be found again (BR-6).

errors.meaning: The school website could not be reached.
errors.notWritten: the item on the site is unchanged and no change is logged
errors.note: Reported rather than appearing to have taken effect (BR-10, AC-10). The integration retries three times first.

planningRules.rule: Never redraft the body. A correction is still the holder's wording (BR-2) — the planner supplies the mechanism, not the words.

Say that the old version was public. It was read before it was corrected, and where it was wrong about a date or a place, the families who acted on it will not see the correction unless somebody tells them (BR-7).
Never call an edit a quiet fix. Every change is logged with what changed, who changed it and when, and the Principal is told — that is deliberate, because it was public (BR-7).
Never suggest restoring an earlier version. The history records what changed; it is not a rollback, and there is no operation that puts the old wording back except editing it back.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An edit cannot be un-made. A further correction is another edit and both rows stay in the history (BR-7), and the wording that stood on the site in between was read by whoever read it. That is the reason the change is logged rather than silently applied.

intent.name: website.item.remove
intent.summary: Take a published item off the site, with a reason. It stays on the record — it was public and may be asked about.

routesElsewhere.note: There is no delete control anywhere. An item is removed from the site and stays on the record, because it was public and may be asked about afterwards (BR-9, E7, AC-9).

request.text: ghalti theek kar do, hatana nahi hai
request.gloss: correct the mistake, do not take it down

routesElsewhere.note: Correcting keeps the item where readers already found it. Removing takes it away from the ones still looking.

request.text: purani cheezein khud ba khud hat jani chahiye
request.gloss: old things should come off by themselves

routesElsewhere.note: Archiving is by age and the System does it, not a person (BR-8) — and the age at which items are archived is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-2). Removal is a deliberate act with a reason.

steps.note: One step. The item leaves the site, the reason is recorded, and it stays on the record (BR-7, BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A removal with no reason is refused (E6), and where the website cannot be reached the item is still on the site and nothing is recorded as removed (BR-10, E5).
plan.atomicity: One write and one outbound call, together: the item off the site and the row in its history with the reason. Removed is where the lifecycle ends — there is no route back up for the same item.

operations.name: website.item.remove
operations.idempotencyKey: item_id, since an item leaves the site once and a repeat is the retry of a removal that did not reach the site
operations.purpose: Remove a published item from the site, with the reason recorded.

parameters.name: item_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No item matches that description. Name it as it appears on the website items screen.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the items that match with their category and the date they carry.

parameters.notes: The item, named the way the writer names it — by its title, its category or the date it carries.

parameters.name: removal_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters, the remover's own. Required (BR-7, E6) — something taken off a public site was seen before it was taken off, and the record of why matters as much as the record of what stood there.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What came off and what stays.

fields.name: item_id
fields.description: The item.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Removed. It is off the site and on the record (BR-9).

fields.name: removed_by
fields.description: Who removed it.

fields.name: removal_reason
fields.description: Why, in their own words.

fields.name: was_public_for
fields.description: How long it stood on the site before it came off — which is how many people could have read it.

fields.name: still_on_record
fields.description: True, always. There is no deletion (BR-9, E7, AC-9).

errors.meaning: No reason was given for removing a published item.
errors.notWritten: The item stays on the site.
errors.note: The reason is what a school has to give when somebody asks where the notice went (BR-7).

errors.meaning: The acting user does not hold the right to publish to the website.
errors.notWritten: The item stays on the site.

errors.meaning: The school website could not be reached.
errors.notWritten: the item is still on the site and nothing is recorded as removed
errors.note: Reported rather than appearing to have taken effect (BR-10, AC-10). The integration retries three times first.

planningRules.rule: Never write the reason. It is what the school says when a family asks where the notice went, and it is the remover's to give (BR-7, E6).

Never offer deletion, and never describe removal as deleting. There is no such control anywhere: the item leaves the site and stays on the record, because it was public and may be asked about (BR-9, E7, AC-9).
Say that removal is where the lifecycle ends. The same item cannot go back up — a fresh item is the route, and that is worth knowing before an event that might be rescheduled has its notice pulled.

Say that people already read it. Something removed from a public site was seen before it was removed (BR-7), so where the item told families a wrong date or a cancelled event, taking the page down does not reach the ones who read it. Telling them is a message, and a separate act (BR-11).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Removal is terminal — the lifecycle has no transition out of Removed, so the same item cannot be put back on the site. A fresh item is the only route, and the removed one stays on the record with its reason (BR-9). There is no deletion to reverse either, because deletion does not exist.

operations.name: website.items.read
operations.purpose: List website items with their status, category, writer and dates.

parameters.name: status
parameters.notes: One of the lifecycle states — Draft, Awaiting approval, Published, Returned, Archived or Removed. The use case defines these in the lifecycle rather than as a fixed value list on the field, so they are carried as written rather than as an enum.

parameters.name: category
parameters.notes: What kind of item. The site groups by it and readers filter by it (BR-6).

parameters.name: written_by_phrase

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. Nobody of that name holds the website permission or has written an item.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the people who match and what each has written.

parameters.notes: Where the question is about one person's items.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.notes: The start of the period asked about.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.notes: The end of it.

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.notes: Archived items have left the front of the site and stay readable (BR-8). They are out of the answer unless the question reaches back for them.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What stands, what is waiting and what has gone.

fields.name: items
fields.description: Title, category, writer, the date published, status and when it was last changed.

fields.name: awaiting_approval
fields.description: How many are sitting with the approver. Nothing here has reached the site (BR-4).

fields.name: published
fields.description: How many are on the site now.

fields.name: archived
fields.description: How many have left the front of the site and stay readable (BR-8).

fields.name: removed
fields.description: How many came off with a reason, and stay on the record (BR-9).

fields.name: approval_required
fields.description: Whether this school requires approval at all — which is what makes an item sitting in Draft either forgotten or simply unpublished (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the website screens.

planningRules.rule: Count what is waiting separately from what is up. An item awaiting approval has not reached the site, and a school that reads one number for both believes it has published something it has not (BR-4).
Never present archived as gone. Archiving takes an item off the front of the site and keeps it readable (BR-8) — it is not a removal and it carries no reason, because nobody chose it.

Say which items are drafts nobody submitted. Where the school requires approval, a draft that was never submitted is invisible to the Principal and is the ordinary way a notice is never published at all (BR-3, OQ-1).
Never report reader numbers. Nothing counts who read an item — the site is read without a login, by alumni and prospective families among others (BR-5, AC-6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

plan.atomicity: A read. The record is append only — an edit adds a row and never rewrites one (BR-7).

operations.name: website.item.history.read
operations.purpose: Return the change history of one item: what changed, who changed it, when and why.

parameters.name: item_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No item matches that description. Removed items are still on the record and can be named too.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the items that match with their category and the date they carry.

parameters.notes: The item, named however the asker names it — including one already removed from the site.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Everything that happened to the item after it went public.

fields.name: item_id
fields.description: The item.

fields.name: current_status
fields.description: Where it stands now — published, archived or removed.

fields.name: changes
fields.description: When, what changed, who changed it and the reason given (BR-7, AC-7).

fields.name: published_on
fields.description: When it first went up.

fields.name: removed_on
fields.description: When it came off, where it did — with the reason (BR-9).

fields.name: approved_by
fields.description: Who approved it, where approval was required.

fields.name: was_public_between
fields.description: The period it stood on the site, which is the window in which somebody could have read it.

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the change history.
errors.note: The history screen is open to the School Admin, the Principal and the Super Admin.

planningRules.rule: Give what the item said before, not only that it changed. The record of what stood there is the point — a school asked why a family turned up on the wrong day has to be able to show what the page said (BR-7, AC-7).
Say how long each version was public. A wrong date corrected within the hour and one corrected after a fortnight are different events, and only the window says which happened.
Never offer to restore an earlier version. Nothing restores; putting the old wording back is a fresh edit and is logged as one.
Return the history of a removed item like any other. It was public and may be asked about, which is exactly why it stays on the record (BR-9, AC-9).

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing. The record it reads cannot be edited by anybody, which is what makes it worth reading.
